title: Sequence padding sensitivity analyzer and deterministic warmup optimizer
author: Priya Shah
description:
Context and motivation: Padding tokens and variable-length priming can change kernel selection and KV-cache behavior in subtle ways that amplify tail latency variance across workloads. Teams have observed non-deterministic p95 regressions when serving mixed-length prompts that are identical in semantic content but differ in padding strategies. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a sequence-padding sensitivity analyzer that synthesizes representative prompt families and measures per-kernel latency/variance across padding strategies, and (2) a deterministic warmup optimizer that generates reproducible warmup sequences to exercise the same kernel paths and KV cache states observed in production.

What this PR contains (single-line sections concatenated into one description): Implements a new runner (bench/runners/seq_padding_analyzer.py) that: generates controlled families of prompts (left/right padding, EOS vs explicit padding tokens, tokenized length buckets), replays them across a range of batch sizes and sequence-length-aware scheduler hints, and records per-request kernel attribution via the lightweight kernel-hint tracer. Adds an exporter (bench/reporters/padding_reporter.go) that normalizes results into newline-delimited JSON with per-kernel p50/p95/p99, tail variance, and a recommended priming length per model/profile. Introduces a deterministic warmup generation script (scripts/gen_warmup_profiles.py) which synthesizes warmup traces that reproduce KV-cache checkpoint patterns; warmups are seedable and include optional priming noise schedules to reproduce production jitter. Adds integration tests (tests/test_padding_analyzer.py) and small fixtures for GPU-local smoke runs. Updates CI bench workflow to include a quick-sample run in PRs and marks the heavy-run as optional manual job. Adds docs (docs/bench/seq_padding.md) with reproduction steps and interpretation guidance.

Checklist: - [x] core runner implemented and unit-tested (local unit smoke) - [x] exporter emits stable newline JSON for downstream aggregators - [x] deterministic warmup seed parameter exposed and documented - [x] CI quick-run added and flakiness mitigations applied - [x] review comments addressed and performance numbers added to PR description

High-level commits: - Implement seq padding analyzer and core sampling harness - Add deterministic warmup profile generator and fixtures - Add reporter that outputs per-kernel quantiles and priming recommendation - Add tests and CI quick-run; update docs and examples

Changed areas (high level): - bench/runners/seq_padding_analyzer.py - bench/reporters/padding_reporter.go - scripts/gen_warmup_profiles.py - docs/bench/seq_padding.md - tests/test_padding_analyzer.py - .github/workflows/bench.yml - bench/fixtures/seq_padding_samples.json - bench/README.md (minor examples update)

Why this is valuable: The pad-sensitivity analyzer surfaces hidden variance sources that cause noisy regressions in mainline perf CI and in customer workloads. The warmup optimizer allows us to reproducibly prime models for benchmark runs and approximate production cache states, which reduces measurement noise and makes small regressions actionable. Together they improve signal-to-noise for CI/regression detection and provide concrete mitigation (priming length recommendation) teams can apply without changing model code.
